newsitem.title: POLAND: Sanok sees net profit up 8 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sanok sees net profit up 8 pct in 1997.

text.p: Polish rubber firm Stomil Sanok SA sees its 1997 net rising to 16.3 million zlotys, up from 15.1 million in 1996, the firm said in a statement on Thursday.

Stomil Sanok said its sales were likely to grow to 183.7 million zlotys, up from 138.5 million in 1996, which would increase the market share of the firm to 45.6-percent, up from current 42.5-percent.
It said it expected its operating profit at 25.6 million zlotys and planned investments of 47.1 million.
It said its consolidated net profit should amount to 17.5 million zlotys, operating profit to 28.4 million zlotys and sales to 202.8 million zlotys.
Stomil Sanok said over 40 percent of its sales would be earmarked for motor companies including its largest customers Fiat Auto Poland and Daewoo Motor Company and also Zasada's subsidiaries.
Other industries targeted by Stomil Sanok were construction and household goods producers.
Stomil Sanok said Germany was likely to remain its largest foreign partner with 60 percent of its export earmarked for the country.
